coverage.boundary: Published OpenID Connect, directly supporting JOSE/SET, and OAuth specifications that can affect a confidential server-side web RP; active framework drafts are included only when they materially describe this profile.
coverage.excluded_families: Digital credentials, native/mobile identity, financial API resource access, transaction authorization and unrelated assertion ecosystems are represented by their applicable umbrella profile or excluded when they assign no meaningful role to this RP.

claim_policy.verified: Every applicable normative requirement for the stated RP profile is inventoried and has the required review and test evidence.
claim_policy.unverified: The implementation exists wholly or partly, but the normative inventory or its evidence is not complete.
claim_policy.not_claimed: The project makes no standards-conformance claim for this item.
claim_policy.not_applicable: The specification assigns no applicable role to this web-based relying party.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 — Authorization Code Flow
standards.scope: Web RP using the Authorization Code Flow
standards.note: Implemented, but no green claim is allowed until every applicable RP requirement is inventoried and evidenced.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 — UserInfo
standards.scope: RP consuming UserInfo responses when configured
standards.note: The optional endpoint is implemented; its complete normative RP inventory is still required.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0
standards.note: Discovery is implemented with exact issuer matching; requirement-level evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework (RFC 6749)
standards.scope: Confidential web client portions used by OIDC code flow
standards.note: Only the portions required by the OIDC web RP profile are in scope; other grants are listed separately.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Usage (RFC 6750)
standards.scope: Bearer access tokens used when DPoP is not negotiated
standards.note: Only client-side use needed by this RP is in scope.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation (RFC 7009)
standards.note: Implemented as a logout cleanup mechanism; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: Proof Key for Code Exchange (RFC 7636)
standards.scope: S256 authorization-code binding for a confidential web client
standards.note: S256 is mandatory in the implementation; requirement-level evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414)
standards.note: The applicable confidential-web-RP metadata is inventoried, validated and negotiated; normative conformance evidence remains incomplete.

standards.title: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices (RFC 8725)
standards.note: Defensive JWT validation exists; the cross-specification normative audit is not complete.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Pushed Authorization Requests (RFC 9126)
standards.note: Supported in automatic and required modes; requirement-level evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Issuer Identification (RFC 9207)
standards.scope: RP validating the authorization response issuer
standards.note: Issuer response validation exists; requirement-level evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security (RFC 9700)

source_review.profile: OAuth client behavior of a confidential server-side OpenID Connect RP using only the Authorization Code flow; authorization-server, resource-server, public/native client, browser JavaScript client, in-browser messaging and unused refresh-token roles are outside this profile.

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1-NO-OPEN-REDIRECT positive: a local post-login target remains usable

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1-NO-OPEN-REDIRECT negative: an external post-login target is replaced locally

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1-CSRF positive: issued state selects its server-side browser transaction

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1-CSRF negative: unissued state cannot reach an authorization transaction

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1-MIX-UP positive: the exact response issuer releases the authorization code

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1-MIX-UP negative: a response issuer from another provider is refused

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1.1-CODE-INJECTION positive: the browser challenge commits to its server-side verifier
RFC9700-2.1.1-CODE-INJECTION positive: the token exchange proves the exact browser verifier

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1.1-CODE-INJECTION negative: state from another browser session cannot inject a code

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1.1-PKCE positive: the confidential client uses the non-disclosing S256 method

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1.1-PKCE negative: explicit absence of provider S256 support fails before redirect

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1.1-TRANSACTION-BINDING positive: each login receives distinct state nonce and PKCE values

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1.1-TRANSACTION-BINDING negative: another provider callback cannot consume the transaction

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1.2-NO-IMPLICIT positive: the browser requests no token-bearing response type

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1.2-NO-IMPLICIT negative: a front-channel access token invalidates the response
RFC9700-2.1.2-NO-IMPLICIT negative: the callback preserves a token field for fail-closed validation

positive.test: RFC9700-2.1.2-CODE-FLOW positive: the token endpoint receives an authorization code grant

negative.test: RFC9700-2.1.2-CODE-FLOW negative: Discovery without code-flow support is incompatible

deviation.rationale: The RP sends an access token only to the issuer's discovered UserInfo endpoint and defaults to identity scopes. Provider-specific claim scopes remain administrator-configurable because the RP cannot safely infer their least-privilege vocabulary or access-token audience.

positive.test: RFC9700-2.4-NO-ROPC positive: token exchange identifies only the authorization code grant

negative.test: RFC9700-2.4-NO-ROPC negative: no provider password credential enters the token request

deviation.rationale: The current profile authenticates its confidential client with a bounded static secret. Asymmetric client authentication remains deferred until OPNsense can provide reviewed per-provider private-key or certificate custody, rotation and deletion without weakening the local recovery path.

positive.test: RFC9700-2.6-METADATA positive: exact Discovery configures the provider endpoints

negative.test: RFC9700-2.6-METADATA negative: metadata for another issuer is rejected

positive.test: RFC9700-2.6-END-TO-END-TLS positive: provider traffic can use its exact HTTPS endpoint

negative.test: RFC9700-2.6-END-TO-END-TLS negative: provider traffic cannot use a plaintext endpoint

positive.test: RFC9700-2.6-HTTPS-RESPONSE positive: an accepted HTTPS origin yields the exact callback

negative.test: RFC9700-2.6-HTTPS-RESPONSE negative: a plaintext authorization response origin is refused

positive.test: RFC9700-4.2.4-NO-THIRD-PARTY positive: callback documents deny every default content source

negative.test: RFC9700-4.2.4-NO-THIRD-PARTY negative: callback policy grants no external network source

positive.test: RFC9700-4.2.4-STATE-ONCE positive: first use consumes the matching state

negative.test: RFC9700-4.2.4-STATE-ONCE negative: replay of consumed state is refused

positive.test: RFC9700-4.3.2-NO-QUERY-TOKEN positive: UserInfo receives its bearer token in the header

negative.test: RFC9700-4.3.2-NO-QUERY-TOKEN negative: the bearer token never enters the request URI

standards.note: The applicable confidential web RP requirements are inventoried and backed by current positive and refusal evidence; reviewed deviations are explicit.

standards.title: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0
standards.note: Implemented when the provider advertises an end-session endpoint; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Front-Channel Logout 1.0
standards.note: Implemented with issuer and session binding; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0
standards.note: Implemented with logout-token replay protection; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OpenID Shared Signals Framework 1.0
standards.note: A bounded push receiver is implemented; stream management and polling are outside the current profile.

standards.title: OpenID Continuous Access Evaluation Profile 1.0
standards.scope: Selected session-affecting events received over Shared Signals
standards.note: Only events that can safely invalidate a local WebGUI session are consumed.

standards.title: OpenID RISC Profile 1.0
standards.scope: Selected account-risk events received over Shared Signals
standards.note: The complete event matrix is audited; seven account-risk events with an exact matchable user subject end only pre-event local sessions.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Session Management 1.0
standards.note: Iframe polling is not required for firewall WebGUI sign-in; explicit and provider-initiated logout are safer fits.
standards.reconsider_when: A supported provider requires session-state monitoring and it can be isolated from the WebGUI.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Dynamic Client Registration 1.0 / RFC 7591
standards.note: Firewall administrators deliberately provision and review a confidential client; automatic registration widens authority.
standards.reconsider_when: A deployment model can preserve explicit administrative approval and credential custody.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Management (RFC 7592)
standards.note: No dynamically registered client is managed.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection (RFC 7662)
standards.note: The plugin is an OIDC relying party, not an OAuth resource server.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628)
standards.note: The OPNsense WebGUI is an interactive browser client.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693)
standards.note: The RP authenticates a browser session and does not broker tokens to downstream services.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Mutual-TLS Client Authentication and Certificate-Bound Tokens (RFC 8705)
standards.scope: Token endpoint client authentication and sender-constrained tokens
standards.note: Certificate lifecycle and a safely bounded HTTP client configuration are not yet available.
standards.reconsider_when: OPNsense can provide reviewed per-provider client-certificate custody and rotation.

standards.title: JWT Profile for OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication (RFC 7523)
standards.note: Useful for providers that discourage static client secrets, but requires signing-key lifecycle design.
standards.reconsider_when: A reviewed signing-key storage and rotation design exists.

standards.title: JWT-Secured Authorization Request (RFC 9101)
standards.note: PAR already protects request delivery for the current profile; JAR adds RP signing-key lifecycle.
standards.reconsider_when: A target provider requires signed request objects or FAPI alignment is pursued.

standards.title: JWT Secured Authorization Response Mode (JARM)
standards.note: The current callback validates state, code binding and issuer without JARM.
standards.reconsider_when: A target provider requires JARM or a FAPI profile becomes a project goal.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396)
standards.note: The RP requests identity claims for WebGUI login, not transaction-specific API authority.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Demonstrating Proof of Possession (RFC 9449)
standards.scope: Sender-constrained access tokens for the confidential web RP
standards.note: ES256 DPoP is negotiated from Discovery, authorization codes and protected requests are proof-key-bound, server nonces are retained without downgrade, and per-provider keys rotate with bounded retired generations. The complete normative inventory is not yet audited.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) Core 1.0
standards.note: The WebGUI uses an immediate browser redirect and requires no decoupled approval channel.

standards.title: Financial-grade API 1.0 — Advanced Final
standards.note: This project authenticates a firewall WebGUI and is not a financial API client.

standards.title: FAPI 2.0 Security Profile
standards.note: The profile targets protected APIs and requires mechanisms outside this WebGUI RP use case.

standards.title: OpenID Connect for Identity Assurance 1.0
standards.note: Local account admission uses stable identity and configured claims, not regulated identity evidence.

standards.title: OpenID Federation 1.0
standards.scope: Federation entity statements and trust chains
standards.note: Each firewall administrator explicitly configures one trusted issuer; automatic trust-chain expansion conflicts with that boundary.
standards.reconsider_when: A deployment requires federation trust chains with an explicit local trust-anchor policy.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Third-Party Initiated Login 1.0
standards.note: The firewall keeps login initiation local so redirect targets and provider selection remain bounded.
standards.reconsider_when: A safe, allow-listed initiation model has a concrete operator need.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps (RFC 8252)
standards.note: The RP is a server-side WebGUI, not an installed application.

standards.title: JWT Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens (RFC 9068)
standards.scope: Resource server validation of JWT access tokens
standards.note: The plugin treats access tokens as opaque credentials and is not the protected resource server.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Form Post Response Mode
standards.scope: RP receiving an authorization response by cross-origin form POST
standards.note: Implemented for providers such as Apple; requirement-level evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: JSON Web Signature (RFC 7515)
standards.scope: RP verification of signed ID, logout and security-event tokens
standards.note: Signature verification uses the platform cryptographic runtime; the applicable validation inventory is incomplete.

standards.title: JSON Web Key (RFC 7517)
standards.scope: RP selection and validation of provider signing keys
standards.note: Provider JWKS consumption is implemented; the normative evidence inventory is incomplete.

standards.title: JSON Web Algorithms (RFC 7518)
standards.scope: Allow-listed asymmetric algorithms used for JWS verification
standards.note: RS, PS and ES verification are supported; symmetric signing and unused algorithm families are deliberately excluded.

standards.title: JSON Web Token (RFC 7519)
standards.scope: RP processing of signed protocol tokens
standards.note: JWT parsing and claim validation are implemented; cross-profile normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: JSON Web Encryption (RFC 7516)
standards.scope: Encrypted ID Tokens, UserInfo or request objects
standards.note: TLS protects transport and the RP accepts only signed protocol tokens; decryption would add private-key custody and algorithm surface.
standards.reconsider_when: A target provider requires encrypted OIDC messages and reviewed decryption-key lifecycle support exists.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 — Implicit Flow
standards.scope: Tokens returned through the browser authorization response
standards.note: The code flow keeps tokens out of browser URLs and is the profile recommended by current OAuth security guidance.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 — Hybrid Flow
standards.scope: Code and tokens returned through the authorization response
standards.note: The server-side code flow supplies the needed login result without exposing tokens through the browser.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials Grant (RFC 6749 section 4.3)
standards.note: The firewall must never collect the identity-provider password; RFC 9700 prohibits this grant.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Grant (RFC 6749 section 4.4)
standards.note: The plugin authenticates a human WebGUI session.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Resource Indicators (RFC 8707)
standards.note: The login flow consumes identity information and does not select among downstream resource servers.

standards.title: REFEDS Multi-Factor Authentication Profile
standards.scope: RP requesting and validating a common MFA authentication context
standards.note: The context is supported together with method evidence; profile-level evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OpenID Connect Extended Authentication Profile (EAP) ACR Values 1.0
standards.note: The phr and phrh contexts are supported together with method evidence; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: Authentication Method Reference Values (RFC 8176)
standards.scope: RP interpretation of bounded signed authentication-method evidence
standards.note: Every registered value is classified as direct, factor-specific or non-elevating evidence; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: Security Event Token (RFC 8417)
standards.scope: RP verification of signed Shared Signals security events
standards.note: Signed SET validation is implemented for the bounded receiver profile; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: Push-Based Security Event Token Delivery (RFC 8935)
standards.scope: Push delivery to the RP Shared Signals receiver
standards.note: Authenticated push delivery and explicit response handling are implemented; normative evidence is incomplete.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications (RFC 10017)
standards.scope: JavaScript applications executing the OAuth client in a browser
standards.note: The OAuth client and tokens remain server-side; the browser is not the OAuth client.

standards.title: Best Current Practice for Security of Cross-Device Flows (RFC 10027)
standards.note: The WebGUI login starts and completes in one browser session.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728)
standards.note: The plugin is not an OAuth protected resource.

standards.title: JWT Response for OAuth Token Introspection (RFC 9701)
standards.note: The RP neither introspects tokens nor validates them as a protected resource.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Step Up Authentication Challenge Protocol (RFC 9470)
standards.scope: Resource server demanding stronger authorization from an API client
standards.note: Authentication strength is selected before WebGUI login; no downstream resource server issues step-up challenges.

standards.title: JWK Thumbprint URI (RFC 9278)
standards.note: DPoP uses the RFC 7638 thumbprint value directly, not the URI form defined by this specification.

standards.title: Proof-of-Possession Key Semantics for JWTs (RFC 7800)
standards.scope: JWT confirmation claims for proof-of-possession keys
standards.note: The provider and protected resource process the DPoP access token confirmation claim; this RP acts only as the presenting client.

standards.title: Assertion Framework for OAuth 2.0 (RFC 7521)
standards.note: Only its JWT client-authentication profile is a potential future fit; assertion grants are outside WebGUI login.
standards.reconsider_when: private_key_jwt key custody and rotation are implemented.

standards.title: SAML 2.0 Profile for OAuth 2.0 Assertions (RFC 7522)
standards.scope: SAML assertion grant or client authentication
standards.note: The provider boundary is OpenID Connect and does not accept SAML assertions.

standards.title: OAuth 2.0 Threat Model and Security Considerations (RFC 6819)
standards.note: RFC 9700 is the current Best Current Practice and explicitly updates the security baseline used by this profile.

standards.title: IETF URN Sub-Namespace for OAuth (RFC 6755)
standards.note: This registry document assigns no runtime behaviour to the RP.

standards.title: OAuth 2.1 Authorization Framework (active IETF draft)
standards.scope: Consolidated authorization-code profile for a confidential web client

deltas.summary: Authorization Code flow incorporates mandatory PKCE parameters
deltas.note: Every login sends a transaction-specific S256 challenge and proves the exact verifier at the token endpoint.

deltas.summary: Registered redirect URIs use exact string matching
deltas.note: The RP emits only exact configured HTTPS callbacks and refuses a callback under another origin or application code.
The RP requests only code and now rejects any front-channel access or ID token even when a code is also present.

deltas.summary: The Resource Owner Password Credentials grant is omitted
deltas.note: The firewall never accepts or sends identity-provider usernames or passwords; only an authorization code is exchanged.

deltas.summary: Bearer token use in URI query strings is omitted
deltas.note: UserInfo receives its access token only in the Authorization header and revocation receives the token in a POST body.

deltas.summary: Public-client refresh tokens require sender constraint or rotation
deltas.note: This RP is a confidential server-side client and never refreshes an access token during the WebGUI session.

deltas.summary: The authorization-code token request omits redirect_uri
deltas.note: The current published OIDC and OAuth 2.0 profile sends the exact frozen redirect_uri for provider interoperability; reconsider only after OAuth 2.1 is stable and the OIDC relationship is resolved.

deltas.summary: Authorization servers support client credentials in the request body
deltas.note: This requirement is assigned to the provider. The RP supports client_secret_post when advertised or configured but makes no server-conformance claim.

standards.note: The design already follows many consolidated security requirements, but the document remains an active draft and is not an RFC conformance target.
standards.reconsider_when: The specification is published or a provider requires a pinned draft profile.
